p-sn46.53-14.1.pi: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, puriso mahantaṁ aggikkhandhaṁ nibbāpetukāmo assa.

p-sn46.53-14.2.en: If they toss wet grass, cow-dung, and timber on it, spray it with water, and scatter dirt on it,
p-sn46.53-14.2.pi: So tattha allāni ceva tiṇāni pakkhipeyya, allāni ca gomayāni pakkhipeyya, allāni ca kaṭṭhāni pakkhipeyya, udakavātañca dadeyya, paṁsukena ca okireyya;

p-sn46.53-14.3.pi: bhabbo nu kho so puriso mahantaṁ aggikkhandhaṁ nibbāpetun”ti?

p-sn46.53-15.1.en: “In the same way, when the mind is restless, it’s the right time to develop the awakening factors of tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.
p-sn46.53-15.1.pi: “Evameva kho, bhikkhave, yasmiṁ samaye uddhataṁ cittaṁ hoti, kālo tasmiṁ samaye passaddhisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, kālo samādhisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, kālo upekkhāsambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya.

p-sn46.53-15.4.en: But mindfulness is always useful, I say.”

p-sn46.53-4.1.en: When the mind is sluggish, it’s the wrong time to develop the awakening factors of tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.
p-sn46.53-4.1.pi: Yasmiṁ, bhikkhave, samaye līnaṁ cittaṁ hoti, akālo tasmiṁ samaye passaddhisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, akālo samādhisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, akālo upekkhāsambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya.

p-sn46.53-4.3.en: Because it’s hard to stimulate a sluggish mind with these things.
p-sn46.53-4.3.pi: Līnaṁ, bhikkhave, cittaṁ taṁ etehi dhammehi dussamuṭṭhāpayaṁ hoti.

p-sn46.53-5.1.en: Suppose someone wanted to make a small fire flare up.
p-sn46.53-5.1.pi: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, puriso parittaṁ aggiṁ ujjāletukāmo assa.

p-sn46.53-5.2.en: If they toss wet grass, cow-dung, and timber on it, spray it with water, and scatter dirt on it,
p-sn46.53-5.2.pi: So tattha allāni ceva tiṇāni pakkhipeyya, allāni ca gomayāni pakkhipeyya, allāni ca kaṭṭhāni pakkhipeyya, udakavātañca dadeyya, paṁsukena ca okireyya;

p-sn46.53-5.3.en: could they make it flare up?”
p-sn46.53-5.3.pi: bhabbo nu kho so puriso parittaṁ aggiṁ ujjāletun”ti?

p-sn46.53-6.1.en: “In the same way, when the mind is sluggish, it’s the wrong time to develop the awakening factors of tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.
p-sn46.53-6.1.pi: “Evameva kho, bhikkhave, yasmiṁ samaye līnaṁ cittaṁ hoti, akālo tasmiṁ samaye passaddhisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, akālo samādhisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, akālo upekkhāsambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya.

p-sn46.53-7.1.en: When the mind is sluggish, it’s the right time to develop the awakening factors of investigation of principles, energy, and rapture.
p-sn46.53-7.1.pi: Yasmiñca kho, bhikkhave, samaye līnaṁ cittaṁ hoti, kālo tasmiṁ samaye dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, kālo vīriyasambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, kālo pītisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya.

p-sn46.53-7.3.en: Because it’s easy to stimulate a sluggish mind with these things.
p-sn46.53-7.3.pi: Līnaṁ, bhikkhave, cittaṁ taṁ etehi dhammehi susamuṭṭhāpayaṁ hoti.

p-sn46.53-8.1.en: Suppose someone wanted to make a small fire flare up.
p-sn46.53-8.1.pi: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, puriso parittaṁ aggiṁ ujjāletukāmo assa.

p-sn46.53-8.2.en: If they toss dry grass, cow-dung, and timber on it, blow on it, and don’t scatter dirt on it,
p-sn46.53-8.2.pi: So tattha sukkhāni ceva tiṇāni pakkhipeyya, sukkhāni gomayāni pakkhipeyya, sukkhāni kaṭṭhāni pakkhipeyya, mukhavātañca dadeyya, na ca paṁsukena okireyya;

p-sn46.53-8.3.en: could they make it flare up?”
p-sn46.53-8.3.pi: bhabbo nu kho so puriso parittaṁ aggiṁ ujjāletun”ti?

p-sn46.53-9.1.en: “In the same way, when the mind is sluggish, it’s the right time to develop the awakening factors of investigation of principles, energy, and rapture.
p-sn46.53-9.1.pi: “Evameva kho, bhikkhave, yasmiṁ samaye līnaṁ cittaṁ hoti, kālo tasmiṁ samaye dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, kālo vīriyasambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, kālo pītisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya.

p-sn46.54-12.1.en: And how is the heart’s release by love developed? What is its destination, apex, fruit, and end?
p-sn46.54-12.1.pi: Kathaṁ bhāvitā ca, bhikkhave, mettācetovimutti, kiṅgatikā hoti, kiṁparamā, kiṁphalā, kiṁpariyosānā?

p-sn46.54-12.2.en: It’s when a mendicant develops the heart’s release by love together with the awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion,
p-sn46.54-12.2.pi: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu mettāsahagataṁ satisambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti …pe…

p-sn46.54-12.3.en: and equanimity, which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go.
p-sn46.54-12.3.pi: mettāsahagataṁ upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ.

p-sn46.54-12.8.en: If they wish: ‘May I meditate staying equanimous, mindful and aware, shunning both the repulsive and the unrepulsive,’ that’s what they do.
p-sn46.54-12.8.pi: Sace ākaṅkhati ‘appaṭikūlañca paṭikūlañca tadubhayaṁ abhinivajjetvā upekkhako vihareyyaṁ sato sampajāno’ti, upekkhako ca tattha viharati sato sampajāno, subhaṁ vā kho pana vimokkhaṁ upasampajja viharati.

p-sn46.54-12.9.en: The apex of the heart’s release by love is the beautiful, I say, for a wise mendicant here who has not penetrated to a higher freedom.
p-sn46.54-12.9.pi: Subhaparamāhaṁ, bhikkhave, mettācetovimuttiṁ vadāmi, idhapaññassa bhikkhuno uttarivimuttiṁ appaṭivijjhato.

p-sn46.54-13.1.en: And how is the heart’s release by compassion developed? What is its destination, apex, fruit, and end?
p-sn46.54-13.1.pi: Kathaṁ bhāvitā ca, bhikkhave, karuṇācetovimutti, kiṅgatikā hoti, kiṁparamā, kiṁphalā, kiṁpariyosānā?

p-sn46.54-13.2.en: It’s when a mendicant develops the heart’s release by compassion together with the awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion,
p-sn46.54-13.2.pi: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu karuṇāsahagataṁ satisambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti …pe…

p-sn46.54-13.3.en: and equanimity, which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go.
p-sn46.54-13.3.pi: karuṇāsahagataṁ upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ.

p-sn46.54-13.6.en: Or else, going totally beyond perceptions of form, with the disappearance of perceptions of impingement, not focusing on perceptions of diversity, aware that ‘space is infinite’, they enter and remain in the dimension of infinite space.
p-sn46.54-13.6.pi: Sabbaso vā pana rūpasaññānaṁ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṁ atthaṅgamā nānattasaññānaṁ amanasikārā ‘ananto ākāso’ti ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.

p-sn46.54-13.7.en: The apex of the heart’s release by compassion is the dimension of infinite space, I say, for a wise mendicant here who has not penetrated to a higher freedom.
p-sn46.54-13.7.pi: Ākāsānañcāyatanaparamāhaṁ, bhikkhave, karuṇācetovimuttiṁ vadāmi, idhapaññassa bhikkhuno uttarivimuttiṁ appaṭivijjhato.

p-sn46.54-14.1.en: And how is the heart’s release by rejoicing developed? What is its destination, apex, fruit, and end?
p-sn46.54-14.1.pi: Kathaṁ bhāvitā ca, bhikkhave, muditācetovimutti, kiṅgatikā hoti, kiṁparamā, kiṁphalā, kiṁpariyosānā?

p-sn46.54-14.2.en: It’s when a mendicant develops the heart’s release by rejoicing together with the awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion,
p-sn46.54-14.2.pi: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu muditāsahagataṁ satisambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti …pe…

p-sn46.54-14.3.en: and equanimity, which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go.
p-sn46.54-14.3.pi: muditāsahagataṁ upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ.

p-sn46.54-14.6.en: Or else, going totally beyond the dimension of infinite space, aware that ‘consciousness is infinite’, they enter and remain in the dimension of infinite consciousness.
p-sn46.54-14.6.pi: Sabbaso vā pana ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ samatikkamma ‘anantaṁ viññāṇan’ti viññāṇañcāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.

p-sn46.54-14.7.en: The apex of the heart’s release by rejoicing is the dimension of infinite consciousness, I say, for a wise mendicant here who has not penetrated to a higher freedom.
p-sn46.54-14.7.pi: Viññāṇañcāyatanaparamāhaṁ, bhikkhave, muditācetovimuttiṁ vadāmi, idhapaññassa bhikkhuno uttarivimuttiṁ appaṭivijjhato.

p-sn46.54-15.1.en: And how is the heart’s release by equanimity developed? What is its destination, apex, fruit, and end?
p-sn46.54-15.1.pi: Kathaṁ bhāvitā ca, bhikkhave, upekkhācetovimutti, kiṅgatikā hoti, kiṁparamā, kiṁphalā, kiṁpariyosānā?

p-sn46.54-15.10.en: The apex of the heart’s release by equanimity is the dimension of nothingness, I say, for a wise mendicant here who has not penetrated to a higher freedom.”
p-sn46.54-15.10.pi: Ākiñcaññāyatanaparamāhaṁ, bhikkhave, upekkhācetovimuttiṁ vadāmi, idhapaññassa bhikkhuno uttarivimuttiṁ appaṭivijjhato”ti.

p-sn46.54-15.2.en: It’s when a mendicant develops the heart’s release by equanimity together with the awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion,
p-sn46.54-15.2.pi: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu upekkhāsahagataṁ satisambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ …pe…

p-sn46.54-15.3.en: and equanimity, which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go.
p-sn46.54-15.3.pi: upekkhāsahagataṁ upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ.

p-sn46.54-15.9.en: Or else, going totally beyond the dimension of infinite consciousness, aware that ‘there is nothing at all’, they enter and remain in the dimension of nothingness.
p-sn46.54-15.9.pi: Sabbaso vā pana viññāṇañcāyatanaṁ samatikkamma ‘natthi kiñcī’ti ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.

p-sn46.55-10.1.en: Suppose there was a bowl of water stirred by the wind, quivering, swirling, and rippling.
p-sn46.55-10.1.pi: Seyyathāpi, brāhmaṇa, udapatto vāterito calito bhanto ūmijāto.

p-sn46.55-10.2.en: Even a person with clear eyes checking their own reflection wouldn’t truly know it or see it.
p-sn46.55-10.2.pi: Tattha cakkhumā puriso sakaṁ mukhanimittaṁ paccavekkhamāno yathābhūtaṁ na jāneyya na passeyya.

p-sn46.55-10.3.en: In the same way, when your heart is overcome and mired in restlessness and remorse … Even hymns that are long-rehearsed don’t spring to mind, let alone those that are not rehearsed.
p-sn46.55-10.3.pi: Evameva kho, brāhmaṇa, yasmiṁ samaye uddhaccakukkuccapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati uddhaccakukkuccaparetena, uppannassa ca uddhaccakukkuccassa nissaraṇaṁ yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti, attatthampi tasmiṁ samaye yathābhūtaṁ na jānāti na passati, paratthampi …pe… ubhayatthampi tasmiṁ samaye yathābhūtaṁ na jānāti na passati; dīgharattaṁ sajjhāyakatāpi mantā nappaṭibhanti, pageva asajjhāyakatā.

p-sn46.55-11.1.en: Furthermore, when your heart is overcome and mired in doubt … Even hymns that are long-rehearsed don’t spring to mind, let alone those that are not rehearsed.
p-sn46.55-11.1.pi: Puna caparaṁ, brāhmaṇa, yasmiṁ samaye vicikicchāpariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati vicikicchāparetena, uppannāya ca vicikicchāya nissaraṇaṁ yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti, attatthampi tasmiṁ samaye yathābhūtaṁ na jānāti na passati, paratthampi …pe… ubhayatthampi … dīgharattaṁ sajjhāyakatāpi mantā nappaṭibhanti, pageva asajjhāyakatā.

p-sn46.55-12.1.en: Suppose there was a bowl of water that was cloudy, murky, and muddy, hidden in the darkness.
p-sn46.55-12.1.pi: Seyyathāpi, brāhmaṇa, udapatto āvilo luḷito kalalībhūto andhakāre nikkhitto.

p-sn46.55-12.2.en: Even a person with clear eyes checking their own reflection wouldn’t truly know it or see it.
p-sn46.55-12.2.pi: Tattha cakkhumā puriso sakaṁ mukhanimittaṁ paccavekkhamāno yathābhūtaṁ na jāneyya na passeyya.

p-sn46.55-12.3.en: In the same way, there’s a time when your heart is overcome and mired in doubt and you don’t truly understand the escape from doubt that has arisen. At that time you don’t truly know or see what is good for yourself, good for another, or good for both. Even hymns that are long-rehearsed don’t spring to mind, let alone those that are not rehearsed.
p-sn46.55-12.3.pi: Evameva kho, brāhmaṇa, yasmiṁ samaye vicikicchāpariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati vicikicchāparetena, uppannāya ca vicikicchāya nissaraṇaṁ yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti, attatthampi tasmiṁ samaye yathābhūtaṁ na jānāti na passati, paratthampi tasmiṁ samaye yathābhūtaṁ na jānāti na passati, ubhayatthampi tasmiṁ samaye yathābhūtaṁ na jānāti na passati; dīgharattaṁ sajjhāyakatāpi mantā nappaṭibhanti, pageva asajjhāyakatā.

p-sn46.55-23.1.en: These seven awakening factors are not obstacles, hindrances, or corruptions of the mind. When developed and cultivated they lead to the realization of the fruit of knowledge and freedom.
p-sn46.55-23.1.pi: Sattime, brāhmaṇa, bojjhaṅgā anāvaraṇā anīvaraṇā cetaso anupakkilesā bhāvitā bahulīkatā vijjāvimuttiphalasacchikiriyāya saṁvattanti.

p-sn46.55-23.3.en: The awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.
p-sn46.55-23.3.pi: Satisambojjhaṅgo kho, brāhmaṇa, anāvaraṇo anīvaraṇo cetaso anupakkileso bhāvito bahulīkato vijjāvimuttiphalasacchikiriyāya saṁvattati …pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo kho, brāhmaṇa, anāvaraṇo anīvaraṇo cetaso anupakkileso bhāvito bahulīkato vijjāvimuttiphalasacchikiriyāya saṁvattati.

p-sn46.55-23.4.en: These seven awakening factors are not obstacles, hindrances, or corruptions of the mind. When developed and cultivated they lead to the realization of the fruit of knowledge and freedom.”
p-sn46.55-23.4.pi: Ime kho, brāhmaṇa, satta bojjhaṅgā anāvaraṇā anīvaraṇā cetaso anupakkilesā bhāvitā bahulīkatā vijjāvimuttiphalasacchikiriyāya saṁvattantī”ti.

p-sn46.55-3.1.en: “Brahmin, there’s a time when your heart is overcome and mired in sensual desire and you don’t truly understand the escape from sensual desire that has arisen. At that time you don’t truly know or see what is good for yourself, good for another, or good for both. Even hymns that are long-rehearsed don’t spring to mind, let alone those that are not rehearsed.
p-sn46.55-3.1.pi: “Yasmiṁ kho, brāhmaṇa, samaye kāmarāgapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati kāmarāgaparetena, uppannassa ca kāmarāgassa nissaraṇaṁ yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti, attatthampi tasmiṁ samaye yathābhūtaṁ na jānāti na passati, paratthampi tasmiṁ samaye yathābhūtaṁ na jānāti na passati, ubhayatthampi tasmiṁ samaye yathābhūtaṁ na jānāti na passati; dīgharattaṁ sajjhāyakatāpi mantā nappaṭibhanti, pageva asajjhāyakatā.

p-sn46.55-4.1.en: Suppose there was a bowl of water that was mixed with dye such as red lac, turmeric, indigo, or rose madder.
p-sn46.55-4.1.pi: Seyyathāpi, brāhmaṇa, udapatto saṁsaṭṭho lākhāya vā haliddiyā vā nīliyā vā mañjiṭṭhāya vā.

p-sn46.55-4.2.en: Even a person with clear eyes checking their own reflection wouldn’t truly know it or see it.
p-sn46.55-4.2.pi: Tattha cakkhumā puriso sakaṁ mukhanimittaṁ paccavekkhamāno yathābhūtaṁ na jāneyya na passeyya.

p-sn46.55-4.3.en: In the same way, when your heart is overcome and mired in sensual desire … Even hymns that are long-rehearsed don’t spring to mind, let alone those that are not rehearsed.
p-sn46.55-4.3.pi: Evameva kho, brāhmaṇa, yasmiṁ samaye kāmarāgapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati kāmarāgaparetena, uppannassa ca kāmarāgassa nissaraṇaṁ yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti, attatthampi tasmiṁ samaye yathābhūtaṁ na jānāti na passati …pe… paratthampi …pe… ubhayatthampi tasmiṁ samaye yathābhūtaṁ na jānāti na passati; dīgharattaṁ sajjhāyakatāpi mantā nappaṭibhanti, pageva asajjhāyakatā.

p-sn46.55-5.1.en: Furthermore, when your heart is overcome and mired in ill will … Even hymns that are long-rehearsed don’t spring to mind, let alone those that are not rehearsed.
p-sn46.55-5.1.pi: Puna caparaṁ, brāhmaṇa, yasmiṁ samaye byāpādapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati byāpādaparetena, uppannassa ca byāpādassa nissaraṇaṁ yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti, attatthampi tasmiṁ samaye yathābhūtaṁ na jānāti na passati, paratthampi …pe… ubhayatthampi tasmiṁ samaye yathābhūtaṁ na jānāti na passati; dīgharattaṁ sajjhāyakatāpi mantā nappaṭibhanti, pageva asajjhāyakatā.

p-sn46.55-6.1.en: Suppose there was a bowl of water that was heated by fire, boiling and bubbling.
p-sn46.55-6.1.pi: Seyyathāpi, brāhmaṇa, udapatto agginā santatto pakkuthito usmudakajāto.

p-sn46.55-6.2.en: Even a person with clear eyes checking their own reflection wouldn’t truly know it or see it.
p-sn46.55-6.2.pi: Tattha cakkhumā puriso sakaṁ mukhanimittaṁ paccavekkhamāno yathābhūtaṁ na jāneyya na passeyya.

p-sn46.55-6.3.en: In the same way, when your heart is overcome and mired in ill will … Even hymns that are long-rehearsed don’t spring to mind, let alone those that are not rehearsed.
p-sn46.55-6.3.pi: Evameva kho, brāhmaṇa, yasmiṁ samaye byāpādapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati byāpādaparetena, uppannassa ca byāpādassa nissaraṇaṁ yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti, attatthampi tasmiṁ samaye yathābhūtaṁ na jānāti na passati, paratthampi tasmiṁ samaye …pe… ubhayatthampi tasmiṁ samaye yathābhūtaṁ na jānāti na passati; dīgharattaṁ sajjhāyakatāpi mantā nappaṭibhanti, pageva asajjhāyakatā.

p-sn46.55-7.1.en: Furthermore, when your heart is overcome and mired in dullness and drowsiness … Even hymns that are long-rehearsed don’t spring to mind, let alone those that are not rehearsed.
p-sn46.55-7.1.pi: Puna caparaṁ, brāhmaṇa, yasmiṁ samaye thinamiddhapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati thinamiddhaparetena, uppannassa ca thinamiddhassa nissaraṇaṁ yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti, attatthampi tasmiṁ samaye yathābhūtaṁ na jānāti na passati, paratthampi …pe… ubhayatthampi tasmiṁ samaye yathābhūtaṁ na jānāti na passati; dīgharattaṁ sajjhāyakatāpi mantā nappaṭibhanti, pageva asajjhāyakatā.

p-sn46.55-8.1.en: Suppose there was a bowl of water enveloped with moss and aquatic plants.

p-sn46.55-8.2.en: Even a person with clear eyes checking their own reflection wouldn’t truly know it or see it.
p-sn46.55-8.2.pi: Tattha cakkhumā puriso sakaṁ mukhanimittaṁ paccavekkhamāno yathābhūtaṁ na jāneyya na passeyya.

p-sn46.55-8.3.en: In the same way, when your heart is overcome and mired in dullness and drowsiness … Even hymns that are long-rehearsed don’t spring to mind, let alone those that are not rehearsed.
p-sn46.55-8.3.pi: Evameva kho, brāhmaṇa, yasmiṁ samaye thinamiddhapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati thinamiddhaparetena, uppannassa ca thinamiddhassa nissaraṇaṁ yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti, attatthampi tasmiṁ samaye yathābhūtaṁ na jānāti na passati, paratthampi …pe… ubhayatthampi tasmiṁ samaye yathābhūtaṁ na jānāti na passati; dīgharattaṁ sajjhāyakatāpi mantā nappaṭibhanti, pageva asajjhāyakatā.

p-sn46.55-9.1.en: Furthermore, when your heart is overcome and mired in restlessness and remorse … Even hymns that are long-rehearsed don’t spring to mind, let alone those that are not rehearsed.
p-sn46.55-9.1.pi: Puna caparaṁ, brāhmaṇa, yasmiṁ samaye uddhaccakukkuccapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati uddhaccakukkuccaparetena, uppannassa ca uddhaccakukkuccassa nissaraṇaṁ yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti, attatthampi tasmiṁ samaye yathābhūtaṁ na jānāti na passati, paratthampi …pe… ubhayatthampi tasmiṁ samaye yathābhūtaṁ na jānāti na passati; dīgharattaṁ sajjhāyakatāpi mantā nappaṭibhanti, pageva asajjhāyakatā.

p-sn46.56-1.10.en: “Prince, there are causes and reasons for not knowing and not seeing.
p-sn46.56-1.10.pi: “Atthi, rājakumāra, hetu, atthi paccayo aññāṇāya adassanāya.

p-sn46.56-1.11.en: Not knowing and not seeing have causes and reasons.

p-sn46.56-1.12.en: There are causes and reasons for knowing and seeing.
p-sn46.56-1.12.pi: Atthi, rājakumāra, hetu, atthi paccayo ñāṇāya dassanāya.

p-sn46.56-1.13.en: Knowing and seeing have causes and reasons.”

p-sn46.56-2.3.en: “There’s a time when the heart is overcome and mired in sensual desire, without truly knowing and seeing the escape from sensual desire that has arisen.
p-sn46.56-2.3.pi: “Yasmiṁ kho, rājakumāra, samaye kāmarāgapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati kāmarāgaparetena, uppannassa ca kāmarāgassa nissaraṇaṁ yathābhūtaṁ na jānāti na passati—

p-sn46.56-2.4.en: This is a cause and reason for not knowing and not seeing.
p-sn46.56-2.4.pi: ayampi kho, rājakumāra, hetu, ayaṁ paccayo aññāṇāya adassanāya.

p-sn46.56-3.4.en: doubt, without truly knowing and seeing the escape from doubt that has arisen.
p-sn46.56-3.4.pi: vicikicchāpariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati vicikicchāparetena, uppannāya ca vicikicchāya nissaraṇaṁ yathābhūtaṁ na jānāti na passati—

p-sn46.56-3.5.en: This is a cause and reason for not knowing and not seeing.
p-sn46.56-3.5.pi: ayampi kho, rājakumāra, hetu, ayaṁ paccayo aññāṇāya adassanāya.

p-sn46.56-5.3.en: “It’s when a mendicant develops the awakening factor of mindfulness, which relies on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripens as letting go.
p-sn46.56-5.3.pi: “Idha, rājakumāra, bhikkhu satisambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ.

p-sn46.56-5.4.en: They truly know and see with a mind that has developed the awakening factor of mindfulness.
p-sn46.56-5.4.pi: So satisambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāvitena cittena yathābhūtaṁ jānāti passati—

p-sn46.56-5.5.en: This is a cause and reason for knowing and seeing.
p-sn46.56-5.5.pi: ayampi kho, rājakumāra, hetu, ayaṁ paccayo ñāṇāya dassanāya.

p-sn46.56-6.2.en: equanimity, which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go.
p-sn46.56-6.2.pi: upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ.

p-sn46.56-6.3.en: They truly know and see with a mind that has developed the awakening factor of equanimity.
p-sn46.56-6.3.pi: So upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāvitena cittena yathābhūtaṁ jānāti passati—

p-sn46.56-6.4.en: This is a cause and reason for knowing and seeing.
p-sn46.56-6.4.pi: ayampi kho, rājakumāra, hetu, ayaṁ paccayo ñāṇāya dassanāya.

p-sn46.57-1.2.en: “Mendicants, when the perception of a skeleton is developed and cultivated it’s very fruitful and beneficial.
p-sn46.57-1.2.pi: “Aṭṭhikasaññā, bhikkhave, bhāvitā bahulīkatā mahapphalā hoti mahānisaṁsā.

p-sn46.57-1.4.en: It’s when a mendicant develops the perception of a skeleton together with the awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion,
p-sn46.57-1.4.pi: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu aṭṭhikasaññāsahagataṁ satisambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ …pe…

p-sn46.57-1.5.en: and equanimity, which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go.
p-sn46.57-1.5.pi: aṭṭhikasaññāsahagataṁ upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ.

p-sn46.57-1.6.en: That’s how the perception of a skeleton, when developed and cultivated, is very fruitful and beneficial.”
p-sn46.57-1.6.pi: Evaṁ bhāvitā kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭhikasaññā evaṁ bahulīkatā mahapphalā hoti mahānisaṁsā”ti.

p-sn46.57-2.1.en: “When the perception of a skeleton is developed and cultivated you can expect one of two results: enlightenment in this very life, or if there’s residue left behind, non-return.
p-sn46.57-2.1.pi: “Aṭṭhikasaññāya, bhikkhave, bhāvitāya bahulīkatāya dvinnaṁ phalānaṁ aññataraṁ phalaṁ pāṭikaṅkhaṁ—diṭṭheva dhamme aññā, sati vā upādisese anāgāmitā.

p-sn46.57-2.3.pi: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu aṭṭhikasaññāsahagataṁ satisambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti …pe…

p-sn46.57-2.4.pi: aṭṭhikasaññāsahagataṁ upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ.

p-sn46.57-2.5.pi: Evaṁ bhāvitāya kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭhikasaññāya evaṁ bahulīkatāya dvinnaṁ phalānaṁ aññataraṁ phalaṁ pāṭikaṅkhaṁ—diṭṭheva dhamme aññā, sati vā upādisese anāgāmitā”ti.

p-sn46.57-3.1.en: “Mendicants, when the perception of a skeleton is developed and cultivated it leads to great benefit.
p-sn46.57-3.1.pi: “Aṭṭhikasaññā, bhikkhave, bhāvitā bahulīkatā mahato atthāya saṁvattati.

p-sn46.57-3.3.pi: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu aṭṭhikasaññāsahagataṁ satisambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti …pe…

p-sn46.57-3.4.pi: aṭṭhikasaññāsahagataṁ upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ.

p-sn46.57-3.5.pi: Evaṁ bhāvitā kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭhikasaññā evaṁ bahulīkatā mahato atthāya saṁvattatī”ti.

p-sn46.57-4.1.en: “Mendicants, when the perception of a skeleton is developed and cultivated it leads to great sanctuary from the yoke.
p-sn46.57-4.1.pi: “Aṭṭhikasaññā, bhikkhave, bhāvitā bahulīkatā mahato yogakkhemāya saṁvattati.

p-sn46.57-4.3.pi: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu aṭṭhikasaññāsahagataṁ satisambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti …pe…

p-sn46.57-4.4.pi: aṭṭhikasaññāsahagataṁ upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ.

p-sn46.57-4.5.pi: Evaṁ bhāvitā kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭhikasaññā evaṁ bahulīkatā mahato yogakkhemāya saṁvattatī”ti.

p-sn46.57-5.1.en: “Mendicants, when the perception of a skeleton is developed and cultivated it leads to great inspiration.
p-sn46.57-5.1.pi: “Aṭṭhikasaññā, bhikkhave, bhāvitā bahulīkatā mahato saṁvegāya saṁvattati.

p-sn46.57-5.3.pi: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu aṭṭhikasaññāsahagataṁ satisambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti …pe…

p-sn46.57-5.4.pi: aṭṭhikasaññāsahagataṁ upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ.

p-sn46.57-5.5.pi: Evaṁ bhāvitā kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭhikasaññā evaṁ bahulīkatā mahato saṁvegāya saṁvattatī”ti.

p-sn46.57-6.1.en: “Mendicants, when the perception of a skeleton is developed and cultivated it leads to dwelling in great ease.
p-sn46.57-6.1.pi: “Aṭṭhikasaññā, bhikkhave, bhāvitā bahulīkatā mahato phāsuvihārāya saṁvattati.

p-sn46.57-6.3.pi: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu aṭṭhikasaññāsahagataṁ satisambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti …pe…

p-sn46.57-6.4.pi: aṭṭhikasaññāsahagataṁ upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ.

p-sn46.57-6.5.pi: Evaṁ bhāvitā kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭhikasaññā evaṁ bahulīkatā mahato phāsuvihārāya saṁvattatī”ti

p-sn46.58-1.1.en: “Mendicants, when the perception of a worm-infested corpse is developed and cultivated it’s very fruitful and beneficial. …”

p-sn46.59-1.1.en: “Mendicants, when the perception of a livid corpse is developed and cultivated it’s very fruitful and beneficial. …”

p-sn46.6-2.1.en: “But what things must be developed and cultivated in order to fulfill knowledge and freedom?”
p-sn46.6-2.1.pi: “Katame pana, bho gotama, dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā vijjāvimuttiṁ paripūrentī”ti?

p-sn46.6-2.2.pi: “Satta kho, kuṇḍaliya, bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā bahulīkatā vijjāvimuttiṁ paripūrentī”ti.

p-sn46.6-2.3.en: “But what things must be developed and cultivated in order to fulfill the seven awakening factors?”
p-sn46.6-2.3.pi: “Katame pana, bho gotama, dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā satta bojjhaṅge paripūrentī”ti?

p-sn46.6-2.4.pi: “Cattāro kho, kuṇḍaliya, satipaṭṭhānā bhāvitā bahulīkatā satta bojjhaṅge paripūrentī”ti.

p-sn46.6-2.5.en: “But what things must be developed and cultivated in order to fulfill the four kinds of mindfulness meditation?”
p-sn46.6-2.5.pi: “Katame pana, bho gotama, dhammā bhāvitā, bahulīkatā cattāro satipaṭṭhāne paripūrentī”ti?

p-sn46.6-2.6.pi: “Tīṇi kho, kuṇḍaliya, sucaritāni bhāvitāni bahulīkatāni cattāro satipaṭṭhāne paripūrentī”ti.

p-sn46.6-2.7.en: “But what things must be developed and cultivated in order to fulfill the three kinds of good conduct?”
p-sn46.6-2.7.pi: “Katame pana, bho gotama, dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā tīṇi sucaritāni paripūrentī”ti?

p-sn46.6-2.8.pi: “Indriyasaṁvaro kho, kuṇḍaliya, bhāvito bahulīkato tīṇi sucaritāni paripūretīti.

p-sn46.6-3.1.en: And Kuṇḍaliya, how is sense restraint developed and cultivated so as to fulfill the three kinds of good conduct?
p-sn46.6-3.1.pi: Kathaṁ bhāvito ca, kuṇḍaliya, indriyasaṁvaro kathaṁ bahulīkato tīṇi sucaritāni paripūretīti?

p-sn46.6-5.7.en: That’s how sense restraint is developed and cultivated so as to fulfill the three kinds of good conduct.
p-sn46.6-5.7.pi: Evaṁ bhāvito kho, kuṇḍaliya, indriyasaṁvaro evaṁ bahulīkato tīṇi sucaritāni paripūreti.

p-sn46.6-6.1.en: And how are the three kinds of good conduct developed and cultivated so as to fulfill the four kinds of mindfulness meditation?
p-sn46.6-6.1.pi: Kathaṁ bhāvitāni ca, kuṇḍaliya, tīṇi sucaritāni kathaṁ bahulīkatāni cattāro satipaṭṭhāne paripūrenti?

p-sn46.6-6.2.en: A mendicant gives up bad conduct by way of body, speech, and mind, and develops good conduct by way of body, speech, and mind.
p-sn46.6-6.2.pi: Idha, kuṇḍaliya, bhikkhu kāyaduccaritaṁ pahāya kāyasucaritaṁ bhāveti, vacīduccaritaṁ pahāya vacīsucaritaṁ bhāveti, manoduccaritaṁ pahāya manosucaritaṁ bhāveti.

p-sn46.6-6.3.en: That’s how the three kinds of good conduct are developed and cultivated so as to fulfill the four kinds of mindfulness meditation.
p-sn46.6-6.3.pi: Evaṁ bhāvitāni kho, kuṇḍaliya, tīṇi sucaritāni evaṁ bahulīkatāni cattāro satipaṭṭhāne paripūrenti.

p-sn46.6-7.1.en: And how are the four kinds of mindfulness meditation developed and cultivated so as to fulfill the seven awakening factors?
p-sn46.6-7.1.pi: Kathaṁ bhāvitā ca, kuṇḍaliya, cattāro satipaṭṭhānā kathaṁ bahulīkatā satta bojjhaṅge paripūrenti?

p-sn46.6-7.2.en: A mendicant meditates by observing an aspect of the body—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.
p-sn46.6-7.2.pi: Idha, kuṇḍaliya, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ;

p-sn46.6-7.3.en: They meditate observing an aspect of feelings …

p-sn46.6-7.5.en: principles—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.
p-sn46.6-7.5.pi: dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ.

p-sn46.6-7.6.en: That’s how the four kinds of mindfulness meditation are developed and cultivated so as to fulfill the seven awakening factors.
p-sn46.6-7.6.pi: Evaṁ bhāvitā kho, kuṇḍaliya, cattāro satipaṭṭhānā evaṁ bahulīkatā satta bojjhaṅge paripūrenti.

p-sn46.6-8.1.en: And how are the seven awakening factors developed and cultivated so as to fulfill knowledge and freedom?
p-sn46.6-8.1.pi: Kathaṁ bhāvitā ca, kuṇḍaliya, satta bojjhaṅgā kathaṁ bahulīkatā vijjāvimuttiṁ paripūrenti?

p-sn46.6-8.2.en: A mendicant develops the awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion,
p-sn46.6-8.2.pi: Idha, kuṇḍaliya, bhikkhu satisambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ …pe…

p-sn46.6-8.3.en: and equanimity, which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go.
p-sn46.6-8.3.pi: upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ.

p-sn46.6-8.4.en: That’s how the seven awakening factors are developed and cultivated so as to fulfill knowledge and freedom.”
p-sn46.6-8.4.pi: Evaṁ bhāvitā kho, kuṇḍaliya, satta bojjhaṅgā evaṁ bahulīkatā vijjāvimuttiṁ paripūrentī”ti.

p-sn46.60-1.1.en: “Mendicants, when the perception of a split open corpse is developed and cultivated it’s very fruitful and beneficial. …”

p-sn46.61-1.1.en: “Mendicants, when the perception of a bloated corpse is developed and cultivated it’s very fruitful and beneficial. …”

p-sn46.62-1.1.en: “Mendicants, when love is developed and cultivated it’s very fruitful and beneficial. …”

p-sn46.63-1.1.en: “Mendicants, when compassion is developed and cultivated it’s very fruitful and beneficial. …”

p-sn46.64-1.1.en: “Mendicants, when rejoicing is developed and cultivated it’s very fruitful and beneficial. …”

p-sn46.65-1.1.en: “Mendicants, when equanimity is developed and cultivated it’s very fruitful and beneficial. …”

p-sn46.66-1.1.en: “Mendicants, when mindfulness of breathing is developed and cultivated it’s very fruitful and beneficial. …”

p-sn46.67-1.1.en: “Mendicants, when the perception of ugliness is developed and cultivated it’s very fruitful and beneficial. …”

p-sn46.68-1.1.en: “Mendicants, when the perception of death is developed and cultivated it’s very fruitful and beneficial. …”

p-sn46.69-1.1.en: “Mendicants, when the perception of repulsiveness of food is developed and cultivated it’s very fruitful and beneficial. …”

p-sn46.7-1.1.en: “Mendicants, the rafters of a bungalow all slant, slope, and incline to the peak.
p-sn46.7-1.1.pi: “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, kūṭāgārassa yā kāci gopānasiyo, sabbā tā kūṭaninnā kūṭapoṇā kūṭapabbhārā;

p-sn46.7-1.2.en: In the same way, a mendicant who develops and cultivates the seven awakening factors slants, slopes, and inclines to extinguishment.
p-sn46.7-1.2.pi: evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satta bojjhaṅge bhāvento satta bojjhaṅge bahulīkaronto nibbānaninno hoti nibbānapoṇo nibbānapabbhāro.

p-sn46.7-2.2.en: It’s when a mendicant develops the awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion,
p-sn46.7-2.2.pi: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satisambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ …pe…

p-sn46.7-2.3.en: and equanimity, which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go.
p-sn46.7-2.3.pi: upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ.

p-sn46.7-2.4.en: That’s how a mendicant who develops and cultivates the seven awakening factors slants, slopes, and inclines to extinguishment.”
p-sn46.7-2.4.pi: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satta bojjhaṅge bhāvento satta bojjhaṅge bahulīkaronto nibbānaninno hoti nibbānapoṇo nibbānapabbhāro”ti.

p-sn46.70-1.1.en: “Mendicants, when the perception of dissatisfaction with the whole world is developed and cultivated it’s very fruitful and beneficial. …”

p-sn46.71-1.1.en: “Mendicants, when the perception of impermanence is developed and cultivated it’s very fruitful and beneficial. …”

p-sn46.72-1.1.en: “Mendicants, when the perception of suffering in impermanence is developed and cultivated it’s very fruitful and beneficial. …”

p-sn46.73-1.1.en: “Mendicants, when the perception of not-self in suffering is developed and cultivated it’s very fruitful and beneficial. …”

p-sn46.74-1.1.en: “Mendicants, when the perception of giving up is developed and cultivated it’s very fruitful and beneficial. …”

p-sn46.75-1.1.en: “Mendicants, when the perception of dispassion is developed and cultivated it’s very fruitful and beneficial. …”

p-sn46.76-1.1.en: “Mendicants, when the perception of cessation is developed and cultivated it’s very fruitful and beneficial.
p-sn46.76-1.1.pi: “Nirodhasaññā, bhikkhave, bhāvitā bahulīkatā mahapphalā hoti mahānisaṁsā.

p-sn46.76-1.3.en: It’s when a mendicant develops the perception of cessation together with the awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion,
p-sn46.76-1.3.pi: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu nirodhasaññāsahagataṁ satisambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti …pe…

p-sn46.76-1.4.en: and equanimity, which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go.
p-sn46.76-1.4.pi: nirodhasaññāsahagataṁ upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ.

p-sn46.76-1.5.en: That’s how, when the perception of cessation is developed and cultivated, it’s very fruitful and beneficial.
p-sn46.76-1.5.pi: Evaṁ bhāvitā kho, bhikkhave, nirodhasaññā evaṁ bahulīkatā mahapphalā hoti mahānisaṁsāti.

p-sn46.76-2.1.en: When the perception of cessation is developed and cultivated you can expect one of two results:
p-sn46.76-2.1.pi: Nirodhasaññāya, bhikkhave, bhāvitāya bahulīkatāya dvinnaṁ phalānaṁ aññataraṁ phalaṁ pāṭikaṅkhaṁ—

p-sn46.76-2.2.en: enlightenment in this very life, or if there’s residue left behind, non-return.
p-sn46.76-2.2.pi: diṭṭheva dhamme aññā, sati vā upādisese anāgāmitā.

p-sn46.76-2.5.en: It’s when a mendicant develops the perception of cessation together with the awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion,
p-sn46.76-2.5.pi: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu nirodhasaññāsahagataṁ satisambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti …pe…

p-sn46.76-2.6.en: and equanimity, which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go.
p-sn46.76-2.6.pi: nirodhasaññāsahagataṁ upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ.

p-sn46.76-2.7.en: When the perception of cessation is developed and cultivated in this way you can expect one of two results:
p-sn46.76-2.7.pi: Evaṁ bhāvitāya kho, bhikkhave, nirodhasaññāya evaṁ bahulīkatāya dvinnaṁ phalānaṁ aññataraṁ phalaṁ pāṭikaṅkhaṁ—

p-sn46.76-2.8.en: enlightenment in this very life, or if there’s residue left behind, non-return.”
p-sn46.76-2.8.pi: diṭṭheva dhamme aññā, sati vā upādisese anāgāmitāti.

p-sn46.76-3.1.en: “The perception of cessation, when developed and cultivated, leads to great benefit … great sanctuary from the yoke … great inspiration … great ease.
p-sn46.76-3.1.pi: Nirodhasaññā, bhikkhave, bhāvitā bahulīkatā mahato atthāya saṁvattati, mahato yogakkhemāya saṁvattati, mahato saṁvegāya saṁvattati, mahato phāsuvihārāya saṁvattati.

p-sn46.76-3.3.en: It’s when a mendicant develops the perception of cessation together with the awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion,
p-sn46.76-3.3.pi: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu nirodhasaññāsahagataṁ satisambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti …pe…

p-sn46.76-3.4.en: and equanimity, which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go.
p-sn46.76-3.4.pi: nirodhasaññāsahagataṁ upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ.

p-sn46.76-3.5.en: That’s how the perception of cessation, when developed and cultivated, leads to great benefit … great sanctuary from the yoke … great inspiration … great ease.”
p-sn46.76-3.5.pi: Evaṁ bhāvitā kho, bhikkhave, nirodhasaññā evaṁ bahulīkatā mahato atthāya saṁvattati, mahato yogakkhemāya saṁvattati, mahato saṁvegāya saṁvattati, mahato phāsuvihārāya saṁvattatī”ti.

p-sn46.8-2.1.en: “Reverend Upavāṇa, can a mendicant know that by investigating inside themselves, the seven awakening factors have been properly implemented so that they lead to living at ease?”
p-sn46.8-2.1.pi: “Jāneyya nu kho, āvuso upavāna, bhikkhu ‘paccattaṁ yonisomanasikārā evaṁ susamāraddhā me satta bojjhaṅgā phāsuvihārāya saṁvattantī’”ti?

p-sn46.8-2.2.pi: “Jāneyya kho, āvuso sāriputta, bhikkhu ‘paccattaṁ yonisomanasikārā evaṁ susamāraddhā me satta bojjhaṅgā phāsuvihārāya saṁvattantī’”ti.

p-sn46.8-3.3.en: That’s how a mendicant can know that by investigating inside themselves, the seven awakening factors are properly implemented so that they lead to living at ease.”
p-sn46.8-3.3.pi: “Evaṁ kho, āvuso sāriputta, bhikkhu jāneyya ‘paccattaṁ yonisomanasikārā evaṁ susamāraddhā me satta bojjhaṅgā phāsuvihārāya saṁvattantī’”ti.

p-sn46.9-1.1.en: “Mendicants, these seven awakening factors don’t arise to be developed and cultivated except when a Realized One, a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha has appeared.
p-sn46.9-1.1.pi: “Sattime, bhikkhave, bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā bahulīkatā anuppannā uppajjanti, nāññatra tathāgatassa pātubhāvā arahato sammāsambuddhassa.

p-sn46.9-1.3.en: The awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.

p-sn46.9-1.4.en: These seven awakening factors don’t arise to be developed and cultivated except when a Realized One, a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha has appeared.”
p-sn46.9-1.4.pi: ime kho, bhikkhave, satta bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā bahulīkatā anuppannā uppajjanti, nāññatra tathāgatassa pātubhāvā arahato sammāsambuddhassā”ti.
